atoms.proposition: the donor is recognised as a charity or CASC for tax purposes
the donor has paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year as the amount of Gift Aid being claimed
the donor has made a Gift Aid declaration that gives the charity permission to claim Gift Aid
the donation is not made through Payroll Giving
the donation is not a payment for goods or services or made because the charity or CASC bought goods and services
the donation is not a payment where the donor receives a benefit over a certain limit
the donation is not from charity cards or vouchers, such as Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) vouchers

limitations: The policy does not specify whether donations from individuals who are not recognised as a charity or CASC are eligible for Gift Aid, nor does it specify whether the tax requirement applies to all donors or only those with a certain level of tax payment.

The policy does not specify whether one-off donations or monthly direct debits are treated differently in terms of eligibility, though it states that Gift Aid can be claimed on donations from individuals.
scope_issues: The policy applies to donations from individuals, but does not specify whether the conditions apply to one-off donations or recurring donations such as monthly direct debits. This creates a potential scope ambiguity.
